advances: The lifted section optimizer can lose depth even when every original fiber has less than half the mass. The original centroid has a proper full-normal minimizing cap and is strictly shallower than another actual point. The example is above the sharper $gamma_2/2$ depth target.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
The integer bases are exactly $-1,0,1$ with section intervals $[0,1],[0,3/2],[0,1]$. Thus the lengths total $W=7/2$, the continuous first moment is $17/8$, and the centroid is $(0,17/28)$. Multiplying each length by $41$ gives the asserted fiber areas and strict inequalities with half the total, $287/4$.

For the minimizing-cap certificate, center the section at its centroid, writing $X=(z,s)$ with $s=x-17/28$. The section support has full affine span and $R=\max|X|\le2$ since $|z|\le1$ and $|s|<1$ on the support. For a unit vector $(a,b)$, the positive moment normalized by $W$ equals $(2W)^{-1}\int|az+bs|\,d\nu$ by zero mean. Pairing the two identical outer intervals bounds their contribution to the absolute integral below by $2|a|$. The central interval contains $[-17/28,17/28]$, which gives a contribution $(289/784)|b|$. Therefore the minimum normalized positive moment satisfies $m\ge289/5488$. With $L=40$ and roof $g=G=1$, one has $Lm/R\ge1445/1372>1$. The centered-section roof realization theorem applies, so the actual cap $t\ge0$ attains raw depth $W=7/2$ over all containing halfspaces and cuts every positive fiber properly.

At $(0,5/8)$, every containing section halfspace can be translated parallel through the point, reducing its mass. An upward through-cap has middle length $7/8$ and outer thresholds $5/8\pm a$ for some $a\in\mathbb R$. The outer upper tails sum to $3/4$ for $|a|\le3/8$, are at least $3/4$ for $3/8\le|a|\le5/8$, and sum to $1$ for $|a|\ge5/8$. In the middle regime the larger threshold is at least one and the other gives a tail of length $3/8+|a|$. Thus the smallest upward mass is $13/8$, attained untilted. For the downward orientation the middle length is $5/8$. The two outer lengths sum to $5/4$ if both thresholds lie in $[0,1]$, and otherwise sum to at least one, since one threshold reaches one before the other reaches zero. A large finite tilt gives exactly one. Pure-base caps give at least $5/2$. This proves the raw section depth $13/8$.

At a middle point with $x<5/8$ a large finite downward tilt gives mass $x+1<13/8$. At $5/8<x\le1$ the untilted upward cap gives $7/2-3x<13/8$, and at $x\ge1$ it gives at most $1/2$. The two outer bases are exposed among the three bases, so a finite base tilt isolates an own interval cap of length at most $1/2$ at each point of either outer interval. This proves uniqueness and also gives the strict section-depth gap at the centroid, whose downward tilted mass is $45/28$.

The original cap $t\ge5/8-x$ contains the lifted section maximizer. On every fiber its threshold lies in $[-7/8,5/8]\subset(-40,1)$, so its area is $W(1-5/8+17/28)=55/16$. Finally, intersect the actual body with its reflection through $(0,5/8,-39/2)$. This retains section lengths $3/4,5/4,3/4$ at the three bases and full vertical height $41$. The subset is lattice-preserving under reflection and has mass $451/4$, so every closed halfspace through or containing its center captures at least $451/8$. The comparison $451/8>287/9$ is exact.
statement: Let $D=\{(z,x):-1\le z\le1,\ 0\le x\le3/2-|z|/2\}$ with $z$ integer, and $C=D\times[-40,1]$. Its positive fiber areas are $41,123/2,41$, each strictly below half the total $287/2$. The section $t=0$ has centroid $(0,17/28)$ and unique deepest point $(0,5/8)$ of raw section depth $13/8$. The section depth of the centroid is strictly less. At the lifted centroid $(0,17/28,0)$, the cap $t\ge0$ properly cuts all three fibers and attains raw depth $7/2$. At the lifted deepest section point $(0,5/8,0)$ the original raw depth is at most $55/16<7/2$. The original point $(0,5/8,-39/2)$ has raw depth at least $451/8>287/9$.
title: A strict no-heavy body where lifting the deepest section point loses depth
